_note: Rule 7.4 — corrections are published, never silent. Append only. A restatement that leaves every figure unchanged is logged as a re-stamp, not a correction, so the correction count stays a measure of wrong figures.

corrections.reason: The scenario converted cubic metres to imperial gallons using the physical constant 219.9692. DEWA bills with 220 — the meter multiplication factor printed on the invoice, and the factor that turns each statutory per-gallon rate into the per-m³ rate DEWA publishes. Source precedence puts the billing formula above a physical constant. Corrected after obtaining Executive Council Resolution 16/2011.
corrections.affected: Dubai water supply, sewerage and total services; the standardized price moves from 9.589 to 9.590 per m³
corrections.also_affected: Sewerage moves from AED 65.99 to 66.00 and total water services from 209.82 to 209.85. The source registry supplied by the publisher applied 220 to water and 219.9692 to sewerage; one city takes one conversion.

corrections.reason: Three frozen rules had stopped describing the engine that produces the figures. v1.0 Rule 3.2 required both headline figures to be published together; the site ships Dubai's water supply while holding its total water services. v1.0 §5 graded a disclosed scope the same as an unresolved assumption, which graded London and Dubai B; the engine grades on uncertainty alone and returns A. The v1.0 §10 fixtures asserted Singapore Grade A at S$ 35.15, London B and Dubai B with per-cubic-metre slabs and VAT on sewerage. None of that was what ran. The change policy in §0 requires an increment; it was not invoked at the time, so it is invoked now.
corrections.affected: Every observation carries methodology_version v1.1 from this date. No published figure moves: Dubai AED 143.85 / 209.85 held, London GBP 46.59 / 79.35, New York USD 28.34 / 73.40, Singapore unpriced. What moves is the recorded grade of London and Dubai, from B to A, and the recorded grade of Singapore, from A to C.

london.basis: metered reference account is scope, not uncertainty; U = 0

dubai.basis: meter type and residency are scope, not uncertainty; U = 0

singapore.basis: PUB publishes its rate table as an image; no tier 1 or 2 source is machine-readable

corrections.prevention: The freeze is now enforced by test/methodology-sync.test.js, which reads the declared block in the document, compares it against src/methodology.js and recomputes every fixture from its stored tariff. The prior CI guard could not fail: it fired only when the document changed, and its condition was satisfied by the engine's own header comment.

corrections.old_value: the part of the game that fails first when water runs short is not the swing — it is the reading of the shot
corrections.new_value: the measure that changed most proportionally was not shot distance — it was the reading of the shot
corrections.reason: The published version asserted an order in which faculties fail as a water deficit deepens. Smith, Newell and Baker 2012 compared two hydration states at a single deficit; it cannot establish an order of failure, and the article's own headline claim went beyond its source. The claim is withdrawn. What the study supports — which measure had changed most in proportional terms by the time body-mass loss reached 1.5% — is stated instead, together with the sample size n = 7, which the published version omitted.
corrections.affected: Standfirst, the section 'The asymmetry', and an added sentence in the opening section stating explicitly that nothing in the piece claims an order of failure. No number in the article changed: 128 → 114 m, 4.1 → 7.9 m and 4.1 → 8.8 m are as published.
corrections.prevention: A study's design limits what a headline may claim. Where a piece turns on one small experiment, the sample size belongs in the body text rather than only in the source note.

corrections.old_value: measurements have mapped perivascular pO2 falling away from the vessel wall, showing the drop-off as a physical fact rather than an inference
corrections.new_value: measurements have reported such gradients, but their magnitude is disputed because the phosphorescence technique can consume oxygen as it measures
corrections.reason: Tsai et al. 1998 was cited as settling the size of the oxygen gradient from vessel into tissue. Golub and Pittman 2008 show that the phosphorescence-quenching method can itself consume oxygen and so inflate an apparent transmural drop. The source is now cited for the existence of the gradient and not its size, the dissenting paper is added, and the animal model is named in the body text.
corrections.affected: The section 'The last micrometre' and the source notes. No figure in the article changed.
corrections.prevention: Where a measurement technique is known to perturb the quantity it measures, that dispute belongs beside the citation rather than in the reader's own literature search.

corrections.reason: Four rules added while extending the engine to ten new cities. §2.5 defines the reference connection, which turns Tokyo's 20 mm and Seoul's 15 mm from assumptions barring Grade A into printed scope. §2.6 fixes one year length at 365.2425 with two narrow exceptions. §5.4 requires both a payable and a structural price where temporary relief is live, and puts the structural one in the basket. §7.6 forbids an unknown component defaulting to zero: every component is observed, confirmed_absent with a source, or unresolved. The index is renamed to the TWJ Urban Water Tariff Index.
corrections.affected: No published figure moves. Dubai AED 143.85 / 209.85 and London GBP 46.59 / 79.35 are unchanged and now carry a declared reference connection. Singapore stays Grade B. New York's arithmetic is unchanged at USD 28.34 / 73.40 but the city is withheld — see the separate entry.
corrections.prevention: The four rules are enforced in src/engine.js and src/acceptance.js and asserted by test/methodology-sync.test.js, which reads the declared block in the frozen document. §2.5's third basis, size_independent, was added during implementation: two of five cities have no size parameter in the residential tariff at all, and requiring them to designate one would withhold an evidenced figure over a parameter that does not exist.

corrections.reason: Rule 7.6, introduced the same day, asked what every silent zero in the base was. New York's record models no fixed component at all. The Water Board Rate Schedule is understood to set minimum charges by meter size for metered accounts, and that has never been read from the archived schedule. Either it sets none for a residential account — confirmed_absent, with the page cited — or it does and must be modelled even where it does not bind at 180 m3 a year.
corrections.affected: New York is withheld with the reason printed where the figure was. The arithmetic is unchanged and still under test: USD 28.34 water supply, USD 73.40 total water services.
corrections.prevention: A rule that only forbids something in prose gets broken by the people who wrote it. §7.6 is checked in the engine and again at the gate, so a city cannot ship by never calling the calculator.

corrections.reason: Rule 9.3, the two-person review, is withdrawn at the publisher's direction and replaced by a publication checklist of seven machine-checkable conditions. The review had one reviewer in the whole system: it held three fully evidenced cities indefinitely while catching nothing, and eight of ten cities showed withheld to a reader when only one was genuinely blocked on evidence.
corrections.affected: Every observation carries methodology_version v1.3. No figure moved on account of the rule change.
corrections.prevention: The loss is recorded rather than glossed: no automated condition can notice that a document was misread, which is what a second human is for. Condition 5 is the compensation — the stored rate must appear verbatim in its own archived capture, which catches transcription between document and record.

corrections.reason: A transcription error. PUB's Annex A prints 1.40 for the block above 40 m3 and the component's own label said 1.40 while the stored rate said 1.42. Found by the v1.3 verbatim check on its first run.
corrections.affected: No published figure changes. The block applies above 40 m3 a month and the standardized scenario is 15 m3, so it never entered a bill and no acceptance test could have caught it. The tariff curve above 40 m3 was wrong by 1.4% on that component.
corrections.prevention: Condition 5 of the publication checklist: each stored rate must appear verbatim in its own archived capture.

corrections.reason: London has been published since collection without ever being checked against a figure its publisher produced. Every other city reaching a publishable grade has at least one such reconciliation; London had none and nobody had looked. Found by the v1.3 publication checklist on its first run.
corrections.affected: GBP 46.59 and GBP 79.35 are unchanged and remain under test. What changed is that they are no longer published while unreconciled.
corrections.prevention: Condition 6: a reconciliation passes, or the record establishes in writing that the publisher offers none.

corrections.reason: §5.3 rewritten. The old rule showed every refusal publicly with its reason, which across ten cities produced a catalogue that was mostly the word withheld — and presented our own unfinished capture as though it were a property of the city's water system. A refusal is now public only where its reason is itself a verified characteristic of the tariff system, the regulatory framework or the source record. Three publication statuses and a required withholding_origin field.
corrections.affected: No figure moved. London, New York, Seoul and Sydney leave the public catalogue as research pending and remain fully computed, tested and recorded internally. Toronto and Abu Dhabi become public exception records with reader-facing statements in place of the gate's internal wording.
corrections.prevention: The test of a public withholding is not how serious it looks but whether the sentence explaining it is about the city or about us. An exception record additionally requires the reason to be established: Abu Dhabi qualifies because the conflict is documented and hashed, not because the question is hard.

corrections.reason: The publication gate treated three levels of proof as one. Source validity and calculation reproducibility are ours to require; external reconciliation is not always available, because a utility publishes a tariff rather than a worked example of somebody else's benchmark. The v1.3 checklist made it a gate condition, which amounted to holding that an official tariff is insufficient until the utility computes our scenario. Blockers are now classed material or validation gap, and only a material blocker holds a number. Validation is reported beside the figure.
corrections.affected: London returns to publication as Grade A with source and calculation verified and no reconciliation, which is now shown rather than treated as a defect. Seoul's meter-size question is resolved as scope under §5.1. Five cities published; four remain withheld and every one is a material blocker.
corrections.prevention: Loosening the gate correctly did not loosen it further than the evidence allows: the prediction was seven published and the outcome is five, because New York's minimum charge, Seoul's and Toronto's tax treatment, Sydney's drought state and Abu Dhabi's VAT conflict each genuinely change the number.

corrections.reason: Three normative additions, each demanded by a city already in the set. §3.8 tariff state: where a tariff selects between published rates on the measured state of the system, the applicable rate is the rule plus a dated authoritative state observation, and a tariff state is structural rather than a temporary policy adjustment. §3.8a trigger provenance: a trigger must come from the instrument governing that tariff. §7.6 gains non_standardizable, because unresolved and known-but-not-standardizable were sharing one word. §5.5 separates publication from index eligibility.
corrections.affected: Sydney's drought rate is remodelled from an assumed component to a tariff state, which puts it in the structural price and therefore in the index once a state observation is captured. Perth's sewerage moves from an ad hoc grade C note to non_standardizable, with the reason that a property valuation is outside the reference scenario. No published figure moved.
corrections.prevention: Modelling the drought as a waiver would have kept it out of the structural price and out of the index, which is exactly backwards: a waiver is discretionary and expires, a drought rate is an existing rule firing on a measured condition.

corrections.old_value: median of standardized bills converted to USD
corrections.new_value: 100 x exp(sum of w_i ln(P_structural_i,t / P_structural_i,base)) in local currency
corrections.reason: The previous construction was wrong in a way collection quality could not repair: a water tariff index must not move because a currency moved. With no tariff changing anywhere and the dollar down ten per cent, a USD-based index reports a ten per cent change in the price of water. Each relative is now a ratio of one city's currency to itself, so there is nowhere for an exchange rate to enter. Geometric because the quantities are ratios: the arithmetic mean of a doubling and a halving is 1.25, reporting a 25% rise where nothing happened.
corrections.affected: No index value was ever published, so nothing is restated. The formula is specified in a new companion document, docs/uwti-index-beta-v0.1.md, rather than folded into the city benchmark methodology.
corrections.prevention: test/uwti-formula.test.js asserts the properties, beginning with the one that made the old form wrong. The obsolete suite was retired rather than adapted: rewriting it in place would have left tests that pass while describing a construction no longer in use.

corrections.reason: The minimum-charge question that withheld New York is closed. The Water Board sets a minimum for meter-billed customers of USD 0.49 per day for water service, plus wastewater at 159% of water charges, frozen since FY2017 and maintained for FY2027. It is not a meter-size charge, which was the hypothesis the city was withheld on — wrong about the form and right that something existed. Modelled as a floor on the bill rather than a component of it, and not_applicable at the reference volume where usage of USD 340.08 a year exceeds the floor of USD 178.97.
corrections.affected: No published figure moves: USD 28.34 supply and USD 73.40 total water services are unchanged. What moves is the price curve at low volumes. The 5 m3 point rises from USD 1.89 to USD 2.982 per m3, because a household using 5 m3 pays the minimum rather than its usage. The floor binds below about 7.9 m3 a month.
corrections.prevention: A curve test asserting a flat New York was written and disproved within the hour by the document that closed a different question. A minimum charge is invisible at the canonical point and decisive below it, which is the argument for publishing a curve rather than a point.

corrections.reason: Three changes the collected cities proved rather than suggested. §2.7: the observation unit is a tariff jurisdiction, not a city — Riyadh and Jeddah are two display cities on one national schedule, and a metropolitan market with several providers is the inverse. §3.9: the price curve is the primary data object and 15 m3 its canonical reference point, because Hong Kong crosses every other city between 5 and 25 m3, Perth and Sydney change places in one currency, and New York looked flat and is not. §7.7: the component ontology is enumerated and a minimum bill is a floor rather than an item.
corrections.affected: No published figure moved, and a regression test keyed on a pre-migration snapshot asserts it for every city that was public. City identifiers and URLs are unchanged. Saudi Arabia enters as two city records sharing one schedule, both research pending on four material blockers that belong to the schedule rather than to either city.
corrections.prevention: Migrated at six published observations. The cost of changing an atomic unit is measured in records, and the alternative was doing it at thirty. One phrasing corrected on review: a single point at 15 m3 does not rank cities incorrectly — it ranks them correctly at 15 m3, and cannot show whether that ranking is a stable relation or an artefact of where it was measured.

corrections.reason: The VAT question that withheld Seoul is closed on the supply side by statute: art. 26(1)2 of the Value-Added Tax Act exempts tap water, and Basic Ruling 26-0-1 defines it as water supplied through conduits by a supplier under the Water Supply Act — which attaches the exemption to Arisu. It was never going to be closed by the silence of a rate table, and Tokyo is why: its table shows no tax line either while its formula multiplies by 1.10.
corrections.affected: Seoul publishes its supply figure at KRW 12,330 a month and KRW 822 per m3, Grade B on the reference connection. Total water services stays unpublished: art. 26(1)2 names tap water and not sewerage, and a sewerage use charge is levied by a local authority under a different act.
corrections.prevention: A component blocker now holds the metric it names rather than the record. §5 already graded per metric and §7.2a already asked provenance per metric; the component state was the third thing that had to follow, and Seoul is the case that showed it had not.

corrections.reason: The first city whose applicable rate required two pieces of evidence rather than one: the tariff rule from Sydney Water and a dated state observation from WaterNSW, the storage authority. Greater Sydney storage is 92%; the drought rate engages below 60%, so the normal rate of A$3.41/kL applies.
corrections.affected: Sydney publishes at A$59.97 supply, A$122.79 total water services, A$3.998 per m3, Grade A. The trigger mechanics remain unresolved and were reclassified from material to validation gap: at 92%, thirty-two points above the threshold and moving 0.1 a week, no lag of any length selects the drought rate. The reclassification is a property of this state and reverts if storage approaches 60%.
corrections.prevention: Applying it exposed that the engine barred Grade A on any unresolved component while the gate honoured blocker_class. Two rules for one distinction is how a methodology drifts from its own code, which is the failure this project keeps correcting. They now share one rule.

corrections.new_value: tests import the payload from scripts/site.js
corrections.reason: npm run build is `node --test && node scripts/site.js && node scripts/render.js`, so the tests run before anything is built, and dist/ is not checked in. test/cross-currency-display.test.js and test/jurisdiction.test.js read dist/site.json anyway. On a clean checkout both failed on a missing file, which means the suite could only pass where a build had already succeeded and CI, which checks out clean on every push, failed on its first step and had been failing on order rather than on anything in the data.
corrections.affected: No figure. scripts/site.js now exports the payload and confines the write and the logging to direct invocation, so importing it computes without writing. The two tests import that value, and therefore check what the code produces now rather than what was last built.
corrections.prevention: test/build-bootstrap.test.js states the property three ways: no test file reads from dist/, a copy of the tree with no dist/ builds end to end, and importing the payload leaves dist/site.json byte-identical. A red that is always red stops being read, which is the actual damage a broken bootstrap does.

corrections.new_value: manifest.captures carries city, date and note; grade and holds are computed
corrections.reason: completed was an append-only log printed by npm run list as a statement of current state. Both readings sat in the file at once: Seoul and Sydney each appeared twice with contradictory lines — Sydney as grade B held by two rules and, four lines later, as grade A held by nothing — and five entries were still held by Rule 9.3, the two-person review withdrawn in v1.3. The generated list closed with a paragraph asking for a second reader nobody wanted, and nothing in the repository could notice, because a hand-written sentence about a rule is checked by nothing.
corrections.affected: No figure and no publication status. The duplicate entries were correct as a log — two captures, two dates — and it was the stored grade and held_by that made them contradict each other. Both fields are removed. The list now derives grade from the tariff record and what holds a city from the acceptance gate, and names the three cities modelled before the log began rather than silently omitting them.
corrections.prevention: test/capture-manifest.test.js restricts a capture entry to city, captured and note, so any field that would go stale fails at the point it is added, and asserts that neither the manifest nor the generator asks for the withdrawn two-person review. Documents that a person must fetch are now an explicit hand_capture flag rather than a paragraph of prose.

corrections.reason: Abu Dhabi raised the question and Hong Kong answered it. Research on the Abu Dhabi tariff proposed that a document dated on the valuation date be required to establish that a captured rate was applicable. Hong Kong water rates have not been revised since 16 February 1995, so no 2026 Hong Kong tariff document exists and none is expected. A rule requiring one would exclude a tariff on the ground that its publisher has had no reason to reissue it, which measures publishing frequency rather than evidence. The practice of treating an open-ended tariff as valid until superseded was already applied to Hong Kong, Dubai, New York and Singapore and had never been written down, so it could not be checked and could not be argued with.
corrections.affected: No figure and no grade. Rule 3.10 states the four conditions and adds valid_through to every record — the date the continuity source was accessed, and not one day further. Six tariffs gained a continuity block; five rest on the publisher's own live schedule, and Dubai's UAE National record, which rests on a 2011 Executive Council Resolution rather than a maintained page, carries a recorded search. Abu Dhabi's continuity source is a page captured 17 August 2026, titled 2025 and last updated 26 May 2025; those three dates are published on the record and are left to the reader.
corrections.prevention: The first implementation demanded a separately recorded search for every open-ended tariff and withheld Hong Kong, Dubai and New York — three records that satisfied every other condition, which is the v1.5 failure exactly. test/tariff-validity.test.js now asserts that Rule 3.10 withholds no city, so the stricter version cannot return without someone deciding to lose those records. Where the evidence is the publisher's live schedule, that schedule is the supersession check; a separate search is required only where it is not, and an unrecorded search counts as silence.

corrections.old_value: Rule 13 covered evaluative claims about prices
corrections.new_value: Rule 13.1 covers evaluative claims about evidence as well
corrections.reason: Rule 13 forbade calling a city cheap, efficient or best on the strength of a small bill, and covered half the exposure. The v1.8 document as first written contained a section headed "The weakest instance is named" about Abu Dhabi, and a correction entry describing one record as the best-evidenced in the Index while others were the least stable. Each statement was accurate and each was about TWJ's own capture rather than about any water system, and each was still wrong to publish: the grammatical subject was a place name, and the place name is the part that leaves the document when somebody quotes it.
corrections.affected: No figure, no grade and no publication status. Four passages were rewritten to publish the evidence instead of a conclusion — for Abu Dhabi, three dates: the page was captured 17 August 2026, is titled 2025, and was last updated 26 May 2025. Applying the new rule to the existing document also found a Rule 4 breach that had nothing to do with wording: §3.9 described Hong Kong as the cheapest in the set at 5 m³, which reads HKD against GBP, USD, AED and SGD. The bullet immediately beneath it notes that Perth and Sydney share one currency so their crossing cannot be a currency artefact, so the same guard was applied one line below and not above. The passage now reports the dimensionless curve ratio, which compares the city with itself.
corrections.prevention: test/register.test.js scans the payload and the frozen document. It tests the subject of the sentence rather than the presence of a word — a verdict term counts only within eighty characters of a place name, drawn from the payload so a new city is covered on arrival — and the section stating the rule is exempt by heading, because a rule must be able to name what it bans. The first version of this check was inert: the pattern was over-escaped and matched nothing, and forty-eight assertions passed against it. It now carries the four sentences that were actually published as specimens it must catch, and three legitimate statements it must not.

corrections.reason: Rule 13.1 as written in v1.8 governed "anything TWJ ships". The check that enforces it reads the Index records, the corrections log and the methodology document, and has never read an article, so the rule claimed a reach its own guard did not have — the same defect this project keeps correcting, in the direction that is hardest to notice, because a rule that overclaims looks stricter rather than looser. The choice was to widen the guard or narrow the rule, and the wider rule was wrong on the merits: the Index is an instrument and the journal is journalism. A comparative adjective attached to a city inside an Index record is the instrument editorialising about its own subject; an article is an argument, and an argument forbidden from characterising anything is not an argument.
corrections.affected: No figure, no grade and no article text. Rule 13.1 now names its scope — city records, grades, withholding and continuity reasons, the corrections log and the methodology document. Articles remain governed by Rule 13 and the evidence standard, which forbid calling water cheap or implying concealment and require a source for a comparison.
corrections.prevention: The declared block carries rule_13_1_scope = index, so the document, the constants and the test agree on the boundary. A separate defect was found in the same pass and fixed: test/tariff-validity.test.js asserted the methodology version that introduced Rule 3.10, so it failed on this bump while saying nothing about tariff validity. A test pins the rule, never the version that carried it.

corrections.old_value: How we check — Two readers, a primary document, an archived copy with a hash
corrections.new_value: the publication checklist, counted from the constants
corrections.reason: The public methodology page described the two-person review, withdrawn in v1.3, and it survived six versions to v1.9 because the sentence was typed onto the page instead of read from the rule. Everything the repository could check agreed with the rule; the one line no test read did not, and it was the line a reader actually sees. The same defect had already been found in the capture manifest, in three city records and in two tests — this was its fifth site.
corrections.affected: No figure. The page now states the seven checkable conditions and counts them from METHODOLOGY.publication_checklist, which travels with the payload, so the number cannot drift from the rule. It also states plainly that the two-person review was withdrawn and why, rather than quietly dropping it.
corrections.prevention: test/deploy-metadata.test.js was added in the same pass for a related reason: two reviews in a row audited the single-file preview artifact and reported missing per-route metadata, social images and Article schema, all of which exist in the deploy tree. The build produces two outputs, only one is publishable, and nothing in the repository said which — that is a defect in the handover, not in the reviews. The test now asserts the deploy tree carries its own title, description, canonical, absolute og:image and Article structured data at every address.
